overview.problemStatement: Roof measurement is an asynchronous, per-report paid provider call, and wirekit has no EagleView module, so every integration re-implements the order lifecycle, polling, PDF download, and its own idempotency; a retried order becomes a duplicate charge, and an unmeasurable address is indistinguishable from a transport error.
overview.proposedSolution: Add an eagleview feature-flagged module exposing EagleViewClient, MeasurementRequest, MeasurementOrder, MeasurementReport, RoofSegment, RoofPitch, and RoofArea: client-credentials OAuth2, idempotent ordering, typed status polling, report fetch, bounded PDF download, and report listing, reusing the crate client, retry, rate-limit, secret, and error types.
overview.targetAudience: Rust developers producing preliminary roofing estimates, including the estimation agent in a consuming application.
assumptions: Commercial contract, API credentials, and report pricing are [to be confirmed]; the caller already holds approved credentials.
The lifecycle is asynchronous: order, status, then report. No status webhook is assumed until the contract confirms one.
Each report costs money; the module never orders without an explicit caller cost acknowledgement.
Turnaround time is unknown, so the module exposes status rather than blocking.
No external research beyond the repository catalogue and constitution (CON-704).
outOfScope: Webhook verification for order status, until a contract confirms a callback exists (RISK-002).
Estimate calculation, pricing rules, and report caching; those belong to the consuming product.
Batch or bulk ordering across addresses.
Historical coverage guarantees for rural or new-construction addresses (RISK-004).

userStories.title: Authenticate with client credentials
userStories.want: the module to obtain and cache a token
userStories.benefit: calls do not re-authenticate every time

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a client ID, client secret, and API base, when the client is built, then both credentials are held in Secret and Debug renders no plaintext.
Given a cached token that is still valid, when a call is made, then no token request is sent, and an expired or soon-to-expire token is replaced before the call is attempted.
Given an address, product, and options, when order_measurement is called, then a POST to the orders resource carries that request and returns an order carrying its provider id and initial status.
Given a caller idempotency key already used for the same request, when the order is submitted again, then the existing order is returned and no second order is created.
Given no explicit cost acknowledgement, when an order is attempted, then the module refuses locally without calling the provider.

userStories.title: Poll the order lifecycle
userStories.benefit: I know whether to wait, use the report, or stop

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given an order id, when order_status is called, then the response is mapped into a typed state distinguishing accepted, processing, complete, and failed.
Given a failed order, when its status is read, then the failure reason is surfaced and the module does not retry the order.
Given a complete order, when fetch_report is called, then the report carries the total area, pitch, and the segment breakdown with each segment type, area, and pitch.
Given a report with a document, when download_pdf is called, then the bytes are returned with the provider content type validated and the body bounded in size.

userStories.title: List reports for a property
userStories.benefit: the same address is not ordered twice

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given an address, when list_reports is called, then the module returns the reports already produced for it, bounded by a caller-supplied limit.

userStories.title: Distinguish provider failures
userStories.benefit: a rejection is never mistaken for a transport fault

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a rejected order, an unmeasurable address, and a processing failure, when each is returned, then the caller can distinguish them by typed error code rather than by message text.
Given a 429 or 5xx, when the call is retried, then Retry-After is honoured, and a rejected order is never retried without being changed.
Given a non-loopback cleartext base URL, when the client is built, then it is rejected as invalid configuration, and the module reads no environment variables.

functionalRequirements.text: The crate MUST expose an additive, default-off eagleview feature that enables no other provider.
EagleViewClient MUST hold the client credentials in Secret, cache the access token, and read no environment variables (CON-519).
The module MUST order a measurement with a caller idempotency key and return the provider order id and initial status.
A repeated idempotency key MUST return the existing order instead of creating a second billable order.
The module MUST refuse to order without an explicit caller cost acknowledgement.
Order status MUST map into a typed state covering accepted, processing, complete, and failed.
A failed order MUST surface its reason and MUST NOT be retried.
A report MUST carry total area, pitch, and per-segment type, area, and pitch.
PDF download MUST validate the provider content type and bound the body size before returning bytes.
Report listing MUST be scoped to an address and bounded by a caller-supplied limit.
Rejected orders, unmeasurable addresses, and processing failures MUST be distinguishable by typed error code.
Retries MUST honour Retry-After for 429 and 5xx and MUST NOT retry a rejected order.
A non-loopback cleartext base URL MUST be rejected at construction (CON-520).

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Credentials and tokens MUST be held in Secret and render redacted (CON-511, CON-519).
Every response MUST be typed and size-bounded before use (CON-515).
All traffic MUST use HTTPS; cleartext must be refused at construction (CON-520).
The module MUST add no runtime dependency.
No application-domain entity may be declared in wirekit; provider schema types only (AC-040, CON-106).

edgeCases.description: An address resolving to multiple structures
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The provider reports it unmeasurable; the module returns a typed unmeasurable error rather than guessing.

edgeCases.description: A report whose PDF is missing but whose measurements exist
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The measurements remain usable; download fails with a typed error.

edgeCases.description: An order polled past a caller-supplied deadline
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The last known status is returned instead of blocking forever.

edgeCases.description: A repeated idempotency key used with a different address
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The mismatch is rejected rather than silently returning the other property order.

dependencies.name: reqwest
dependencies.notes: Already compiled in with rustls-tls; reused unchanged.

dependencies.name: serde_json
dependencies.notes: Already present; request and report payloads.

risks.description: EagleView commercial contract and API credentials are unconfirmed.
risks.mitigation: Build and verify against a local mock; keep the assumption marked [to be confirmed].

risks.description: No order-status webhook is assumed to exist.
risks.mitigation: Poll with bounded backoff; add verification in a later version only if the contract confirms a callback.
Require an explicit caller cost acknowledgement, so no unpriced order can be placed.

risks.description: Coverage gaps for rural or new-construction addresses.
risks.mitigation: Surface a typed unmeasurable error rather than a generic failure.
